comment:
<comment datatype="string"><a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=G1G01-2702-MONOMER">Gallate dioxygenase</a> is a ring-cleavage dioxygenase that acts specifically on <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=CPD-183">gallate</a> to produce the keto-tautomer of 4-oxalomesaconate [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16030014">Nogales05</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/21219457">Nogales10</a>]. The protein is a homotrimer and uses <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=FE%2b2">Fe<sup>2+</sup></a> as the main cofactor. 
The enzyme shares a common ancestor with <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CPLX-7916">protocatechuate 4,5-dioxygenase</a>, and has a two-domain architecture that might have evolved from the fusion of the large and small subunits of the latter.
<p>
Expression of the <a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=G1G01-2702">gllA</a> gene was induced when <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=TAX-160488"><i>Pseudomonas putida</i> KT2440</a> cells grew in the presence of gallate [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16030014">Nogales05</a>].
The gene was cloned and expressed in <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=TAX-562"><i>Escherichia coli</i></a>, and the recombinant protein was piurified to homogeneity [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16030014">Nogales05</a>].</comment>
